newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- HAMBROS CHIEF APOLOGISES TO CO-OP

Hambros Bank has issued a top-level apology to the Co- operative Wholesale Society (CWS) over its involvement with Andrew Regan, the businessman who was forced to abort an attempted takeover bid for the CWS last week. Hambros was involved in copying confidential CWS documents and circulating them to leading banks and other financial firms. The public apology follows the disclosure of Hambros's role in the affair in the High Court last week.
-- DEMON INTERNET SEARCHES FOR A STRATEGIC INVESTOR

Demon Internet, the independent Internet service provider, has approached a number of potential buyers as it seeks a strategic investor. Demon, the UK's largest Internet service provider, has written to about half a dozen possible investors offering them a stake of up to 49 per cent. The move has been seen as confirmation of the consolidation taking place in the Internet access market.
-- EAST EUROPEAN STEEL PRICES NOW MATCH EU LEVELS

The price of sheet steel in eastern Europe has reached the same levels as in the west for the first time since the Second World War. The convergence in steel prices - a staple industrial raw material - has been seen as reflecting the long-term economic transformation of eastern Europe, as well as recent short-term swings in supply and demand between the two regions.
-- DIGITAL ADVANCE 'SPELLS END FOR CORDED PHONES'

A new study from management consultants Roland Berger & Partners has forecast the end of the corded telephone. The study suggests that cordless handsets, which offer the latest in digital technology, will replace the older standard as the price of the new sets falls. It predicts that annual sales of cordless telephones designed around the DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephone) standard will rise in the UK from 200,000 units in 1995-96 to 2.2 million units, or 20 per cent of the UK handset market by 1999-2000.
-- CHANNEL 5 TO BOOST MARKETING

Channel 5 has announced plans for a marketing campaign in May aimed at attempting to persuade more people to tune to the newly-launched terrestrial channel. The move follows an opinion poll which found that 14 per cent of viewers in areas covered by Channel 5 transmitters were experiencing some sort of reception problems. The second phase of the marketing campaign will attempt to persuade these viewers to consult aerial companies.
-- RENEWED UPTURN IN CONSUMER OPTIMISM

A new survey from consultants Business Strategies has found consumer confidence to be higher now than at any time since the late 1980s in all regions of the UK, except Northern Ireland. The research, the latest quarterly analysis compiled from monthly polls from a market research company, shows that the rate at which confidence is increasing has picked up.
-- HALIFAX WARNS OF SHARES CHAOS

Electronic share settlement system Crest may face a collapse following the 13 billion stg Halifax flotation which led to a surge of early share sales by members of the banking society. The heavy volume of action may cause problems to phone lines and stockbrokers as well. Analysts are predicting a five pound per share opening trading price and Halifax has advised shareholders to refrain from selling immediately.
-- BSM SAYS NEW TEST RULES WILL LEAD TO PROFITS FALL

UK driving school group BSM has announced it will close 18 of its 154 branches, a result of revised driving test rules which the school believes will halve its interim profits. A profits warning from the company led to a 38p fall in share prices to 103 1/2p compared with 170p in 1993. The cuts, which are hoped to save one million dollars, may cause up to 20 redundancies. The company's pre-tax profits for 1996 were 2.9 million sterling.
-- MURDOCH HITS SNAG IN PLANNED ECHOSTAR LINK

Applications for regulatory approval of Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation's one billion prospective investment in Colorado-based EchoStar have been delayed amid speculation in EchoStar that the media tycoon would not adhere to its obligations. The move means a setback for Murdoch, who had planned to get a head start in the US satellite television market. The major issue of discord concerns News Corp's demand that EchoStar abandon its own smart card and set-top box system.
-- KALAMAZOO ADMITS SALES DATA FALSIFIED

Following reports that two managers of accounting software producer Kalamazoo Computer had falsified internal accounts, the group experienced a sharp share plunge. The employees names will not be released as Kalamazoo chairman Bob Jordan said the company did not profit from the errors and lost no money. The computer group did warn accounting errors meant it would not meet expectations of a one million sterling rise over 1996 profits.
